claims.claim: In Yun et al.'s WritingPrompts task the semantic diversity was 0.3291 under the full chat template, 0.4767 under a simple steer prompt and 0.3427 under the template with an explicit diversity instruction.
claims.source: Yun, An, Wang, Peng and Shang (UC San Diego), arXiv 2505.18949 v1

claims.claim: Gerstgrasser et al. demonstrate that accumulating successive generations of synthetic data alongside the original real data avoids model collapse.
claims.source: Gerstgrasser, Schaeffer, Dey, Rafailov et al. (Stanford and others), arXiv 2404.01413
claims.quote: generations of synthetic data alongside the original real data avoids model

claims.claim: Gerstgrasser et al. confirm that replacing the original real data by each generation's synthetic data does tend towards model collapse.
claims.source: Gerstgrasser, Schaeffer, Dey, Rafailov et al. (Stanford and others), arXiv 2404.01413
claims.quote: the original real data by each generation

claims.claim: Murthy, Ullman and Hu found aligned models generally display less conceptual diversity than their instruction fine-tuned counterparts.
claims.source: Murthy, Ullman and Hu (Harvard / Kempner Institute), arXiv 2411.04427
claims.quote: display less diversity than their instruction fine-

claims.claim: Murthy, Ullman and Hu report that no model in their study reached human-like conceptual diversity.
claims.source: Murthy, Ullman and Hu (Harvard / Kempner Institute), arXiv 2411.04427

claims.claim: Shypula et al. find that preference-tuned models exhibit greater effective semantic diversity than SFT or base models once quality thresholds are applied.
claims.source: Shypula, Li, Zhang, Padmakumar, Yin and Bastani (Penn / NYU / Berkeley), COLM 2025
claims.quote: models exhibit greater effective semantic diversity

claims.claim: Shypula et al. found that restricted to high-quality generations only, preference-tuned models produce less semantically diverse content within that subset.
claims.source: Shypula, Li, Zhang, Padmakumar, Yin and Bastani (Penn / NYU / Berkeley), COLM 2025
claims.quote: duce less semantically diverse content within that subset

claims.claim: Shypula et al. report that for open-ended creative writing preference tuning is linked to greater diversity in lexical patterns.
claims.source: Shypula, Li, Zhang, Padmakumar, Yin and Bastani (Penn / NYU / Berkeley), COLM 2025
claims.quote: preference tuning is linked to greater diversity in lexical patterns

claims.claim: Chung et al. report that their trained models had higher diversity than GPT-4o-iter, a baseline that used diversity-inducing prompts.
claims.source: Chung, Padmakumar, Roemmele, Sun and Kreminski (Midjourney / NYU), arXiv 2503.17126
claims.quote: even higher than •GPT-4o-iter, which used diversity-inducing prompts

claims.claim: Chung et al. report that human-crafted gold stories scored lower on their reward model than the instruction-tuned models but were far more diverse.
claims.source: Chung, Padmakumar, Roemmele, Sun and Kreminski (Midjourney / NYU), arXiv 2503.17126
claims.quote: these models but the diversity was far higher

claims.claim: Chung et al. report an 8B-parameter model trained with their deviation-weighted objective achieving diversity on par with a human-created dataset.
claims.source: Chung, Padmakumar, Roemmele, Sun and Kreminski (Midjourney / NYU), arXiv 2503.17126
claims.quote: achieve on-par diversity as a human-created

claims.claim: Xiao et al. argue the Kullback-Leibler-based regularization in RLHF carries an algorithmic bias that in extreme cases produces preference collapse.
claims.source: Xiao, Li, Xie, Getzen, Fang, Long and Su, Journal of the American Statistical Association (arXiv 2405.16455 v2)
claims.quote: this bias could lead to a phenomenon we term preference collapse

claims.claim: Xiao et al. report their preference-matching RLHF variant improved alignment with human preferences by 29% to 41% over standard RLHF on one metric.
claims.source: Xiao, Li, Xie, Getzen, Fang, Long and Su, Journal of the American Statistical Association (arXiv 2405.16455 v2)

claims.claim: janus, who coined the mode-collapse usage, later corrected the post to say text-davinci-002 was not trained with RLHF.
claims.source: janus, 'Mysteries of mode collapse', LessWrong / AI Alignment Forum, 8 November 2022, with the author's later correction note
claims.quote: text-davinci-002 was not trained with RLHF

claims.claim: janus argues that raising the sampling temperature flattens the rest of the output distribution into undifferentiated goo before it helps escape a high-confidence attractor.
claims.source: janus, 'Mysteries of mode collapse', LessWrong / AI Alignment Forum, 8 November 2022
claims.quote: will flatten the rest of the output distribution into undifferentiated goo
